I am an old man now, 62 years, and I have been farming this land in the North West for many years. On my small plot of less than one hectare, I plant millet with cowpea between the rows like my fathers did — the cowpea helps the soil and feeds my household. I will buy a little urea from the market if the rains come well, because millet gives better heads with some fertilizer, but I cannot afford much on this small plot. I keep some goats and chickens, so I spread their droppings on the field before the rains, and I save my own seed from last year's harvest because the improved seeds from town are costly and not always suited to our dry land.
